Task: rank the five most likely patients, most likely first, with a probability for each (they need not sum to one). For each, say which findings in the report support the placement and which argue against it, counting recorded absences as evidence; keep each to one or two sentences. Then say what the report lacked that would have made you more confident.

ranking.for: Demonstrates cessation of head growth (the hallmark progressive microcephaly), hypertonia/bulbar palsy, and prominent brain anomalies including delayed CNS myelination, thin corpus callosum, and ventriculomegaly.
ranking.against: Seizures are not explicitly documented in the observed phenotype despite being frequently associated with PLAA-related encephalopathy.

ranking.for: Features microcephaly, spasticity, thin corpus callosum, global developmental delay, and hypsarrhythmia consistent with severe epileptic encephalopathy.
ranking.against: Seizures and appendicular spasticity are explicitly recorded as absent, and microcephaly is not specified as progressive.

ranking.for: Presents with microcephaly, thin corpus callosum, brisk reflexes/Babinski sign reflecting upper motor neuron involvement, and generalized seizures.
ranking.against: Lacks explicit confirmation of progressive leukoencephalopathy or delayed myelination, and the clinical description is relatively sparse.

ranking.for: Has microcephaly, spasticity, seizures, thin corpus callosum, and white matter involvement (periventricular leukomalacia).
ranking.against: Extensive hemorrhages (intracranial, vitreous, preretinal) and preterm birth point strongly toward COL4A1/vascular perinatal pathology rather than primary PLAA deficiency.

ranking.for: Shows epileptic encephalopathy with epileptic spasms and global developmental delay.
ranking.against: Key cardinal features of PLAA including thin corpus callosum, cerebral atrophy, and delayed myelination are explicitly recorded as absent.

rounds.what_the_report_lacked: Serial occipital frontal circumference (OFC) trajectory measurements to definitively capture the postnatal progressive nature of the microcephaly, as well as specific neuroimaging details on white matter loss/leukoencephalopathy progression.

ranking.for: Presents with the disease's core triad of microcephaly, spasticity, and brain anomalies (thin corpus callosum), alongside hypsarrhythmia indicating epileptic encephalopathy and optic disc pallor.
ranking.against: Seizure is recorded as absent despite hypsarrhythmia, and appendicular spasticity is listed as absent despite generalized spasticity.

ranking.for: Features microcephaly, thin corpus callosum, seizures with interictal EEG abnormalities, and signs of upper motor neuron involvement (brisk reflexes, Babinski sign).
ranking.against: Lacks an explicit diagnosis of spasticity and documentation of progressive leukoencephalopathy or optic nerve involvement.

ranking.for: Demonstrates progressive microcephaly (cessation of head growth), brain anomalies (thin corpus callosum, delayed myelination, abnormal gyration), bulbar palsy, and optic atrophy.
ranking.against: The presence of postaxial polydactyly and pedal edema strongly suggests an alternative syndromic diagnosis such as a ciliopathy.

ranking.for: Exhibits microcephaly, spasticity, thin corpus callosum, seizures, and white matter involvement (periventricular leukomalacia).
ranking.against: Extensive intracranial, retinal, and vitreous hemorrhages along with retinal arterial tortuosity are indicative of a vascular collagenopathy rather than NDMSBA.

ranking.for: Demonstrates early-onset epileptic encephalopathy with epileptic spasms and severe neurodevelopmental impairment.
ranking.against: Key cardinal features of the disorder, specifically thin corpus callosum, delayed CNS myelination, and optic atrophy, are documented as absent.

rounds.what_the_report_lacked: Serial occipital frontal circumference measurements to document whether the microcephaly was progressive/postnatal in onset, neuroimaging details explicitly characterizing progressive leukoencephalopathy/hypomyelination, and confirmation of biallelic pathogenic variants in PLAA.

ranking.for: Demonstrates the core triad defining the condition: microcephaly, spasticity, and brain anomalies (thin corpus callosum), along with epileptic features (hypsarrhythmia), optic disc pallor, global developmental delay, and axial hypotonia.
ranking.against: Recorded absence of overt clinical seizures (despite hypsarrhythmia) and appendicular spasticity.

ranking.for: Features microcephaly, structural brain abnormality (thin corpus callosum), seizures with interictal EEG abnormalities, and upper motor neuron signs (Brisk reflexes, Babinski sign).
ranking.against: Lacks an explicit finding of spasticity (only hypotonia and hyperreflexia noted) and has no documented progressive course or leukoencephalopathy.

ranking.for: Presents with progressive microcephaly (cessation of head growth), multiple brain anomalies (delayed myelination, thin corpus callosum, ventriculomegaly), hypertonia, and optic atrophy.
ranking.against: Presence of postaxial polydactyly and edema of the feet strongly points toward an alternative syndromic diagnosis.

ranking.for: Exhibits microcephaly, spasticity, seizures, severe global developmental delay, and white matter/brain anomalies (thin corpus callosum, periventricular leukomalacia).
ranking.against: Presence of intracranial and retinal hemorrhages with retinal arterial tortuosity is characteristic of COL4A1/2-related angiopathy rather than PLAA deficiency.

ranking.for: Exhibits early-onset epileptic encephalopathy with epileptic spasms and global developmental delay.
ranking.against: Recorded absence of microcephaly, thin corpus callosum, delayed CNS myelination, and optic atrophy.

rounds.what_the_report_lacked: The report lacked detailed neuroimaging follow-up documenting progressive leukoencephalopathy, specific age-of-onset records for microcephaly to demonstrate its progressive nature, and targeted genetic testing data for the PLAA gene.
